Judgment

1. This is a Criminal Appeal under Section 374 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, directed against judgment dated 25.01.2020 and order on sentence dated 13.03.2020 passed by the Court of Ld. Metropolitan Magistrate-03 (West), Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi in a case bearing FIR No.
272/2005 PS Mayapuri under Section 420/468/471/120B of IPC.

entities.text: Metropolitan Magistrate-03 (West), Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Notice of the appeal was served upon the respondent / State.
During arguments, it was stated by appellant that he had settled the matter with the complainant / victim during the trial.

Accordingly,
notice was issued to the complainant, namely Smt.Neelam Jain.

3. Trial Court Record was summoned and arguments were heard.
4. Perusal of Trial Court Record reveals that accused that on a complaint case under Section 156(3)
Cr.P.C. filed by the complainant Smt. Neelam Jain, Ld. Metropolitan Magistrate vide order dated 29.09.2005 directed registration of FIR.
Accordingly, FIR No. 272/2005 PS Mayapuri under Section 420/468/471/120B of IPC was registered.
After investigation, charge sheet was filed against one Kulbhushan Jain, one Rajender and the present appellant, namely Chokhe Lal.
After examination of prosecution witnesses, statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. were recorded.
5. During trial, accused Rajender expired and proceedings against him abated vide order dated 12.10.2016.

1
6. Vide impugned judgment, the Trial Court convicted Kulbhushan Jain and appellant Chokhe Lal under Section 420/120B IPC only.
However, they were acquitted for offences under Section 468/471 IPC.

7. Vide impugned order on sentence dated 13.03.2020, convict Kulbhushan Jain and appellant were sentenced to Simple Imprisonment for two years under Section 420 IPC and they were sentenced to Simple Imprisonment for one year under Section 120B IPC.
8.
Kulbhushan Jain was directed to pay compensation of Rs.2,50,000/- to the complainant and appellant Chokhe Lal was directed to pay a compensation of Rs.50,000/- to complainant.
9. Said Kulbhushan Jain however lateron expired on 14.05.2020.
Therefore, the present appeal has been filed by appellant Chokhe Lal only.

10. Perusal of the testimony of complainant Smt. Neelam Jain (PW-1) shows that accused Kulbhushan Jain, a property dealer induced her to purchase a plot No. 182 in Khasra No. 427,
Bhagat Singh Park, Siraspur and he introduced appellant Chokhe Lal as its owner and accused Rajender as its co-owner.
The complainant (PW-1) made a payment of Rs. 10,000/- to accused persons on 25.04.2005 and thereafter, a sum of Rs.2,50,000/- on 26.04.2005.
Documents were executed.
However, later she came to know that accused Chokhe Lal was not the real owner of the plot.
Sh. Parveen Kumar Jain (PW-2) supported PW-1 in his evidence.
11. I am not inclined to discuss further evidence because the issue of cheating is proved by these two witnesses as per prosecution evidence.
It is argued by ld.
Counsel for appellant that Chokhe Lal is an extremely poor person and he was used by Kulbhushan Jain and Rajender while taking undue advantage of his simplicity.
It is argued by ld.
Counsel for appellant that in her evidence, PW-1 has testified that Chokhe Lal was introduced as a owner of the plot by Kulbhushan and Rajender.

This shows that main offenders were the said persons, who were property dealers and not Chokhe Lal,
who is extremely poor person.
Therefore, it is argued that benefit of doubt should be given to the appellant.
12. Ld. Addl. PP argued that appellant was an active participant in the criminal conspiracy with other accused persons and no benefit can be given to him.
13. I have considered the rival submissions and perused the testimony of all the witnesses.
In the entire cross-examination of PW-1, PW-2 and the Investigating Officer, it has not been put to the said witnesses that appellant himself was the owner of the plot in question.
Nothing is coming out from the cross- examination that he was a victim of circumstances and was used by his co-accused persons because of his simplicity.

In these circumstances, I find no substance in the arguments of ld.
Counsel for the appellant.
The impugned judgment of conviction of appellant under Section 420/120B IPC is a well reasoned judgment and I find no infirmity in the same.
14. Now, I take up the issue of quantum of sentence.
The complainant has filed an application for compounding the offence which was dismissed due to the nature of offence.

"Statement of Smt. Neelam Jain, w/o. Late Sh. Parveen Kumar Jain, aged 64 years,

sentences.text: r/o. WZ-315/5A, Hari Nagar, G-Block Extension, Jail Road, Delhi.
On SA I am complainant in the present case.
The matter has already been settled in the present case and for the purpose of settlement, the appellant had issued a cheque which was dishonoured.

Therefore, I had filed a complaint case (CC No. 3632/12 titled 'Neelam Jain vs. Chokhe Lal') before Sh. Gagandeep Jindal, Ld. MM (South West) wherein on 22.06.2013, the accused/appellant Chokhe Lal had paid a sum of Rs 2,50,000/- to me.

entities.text: CC No. 3632/12 titled 'Neelam Jain vs. Chokhe Lal
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the said complaint was compounded and appellant was acquitted.
This amount was basically a settlement for the present case.

Today, I have voluntarily compromised / settled the present offence with the appellant namely Chokhe Lal, s/o. Late Sh.Madan Lal and I have moved the application through my counsel with a request to accord permission to compound the offence.
It may please be allowed.
Today also, the appellant has further paid an agreed amount of Rs.10,000/- to me.

The application is Ex. P-1 bearing my signature at point A."
15.
Ld. counsel for appellant submits that appellant is an extremely poor person but still has made payment of the cheated amount to complainant.
Thus, the complainant has been sufficiently compensated and she is satisfied.
It is further submitted that although the complainant wanted to compound the offence but permission was not given by this Court.

It is further submitted that the appellant has remained in the Judicial Custody w.e.f. 29.01.2006 to 21.03.2006 for 52 days and w.e.f. 07.09.2006 to 30.10.2006 for 53 days (i.e. in total for 105 days).

Further after conviction,
appellant was taken into custody on 15.12.2020 and remained in jail till 16.06.2021.
It is submitted that the appellant has suffered a protracted and long trial.
Therefore, it is prayed that a lenient view may be taken.
16. Ld. Addl. PP has strongly opposed a lenient in view of serious nature of offence.
17. I have considered the rival submissions.
I am of the opinion that the appellant who appears to be a very poor person has compensated complainant sufficiently.
He has remained in judicial custody for the period already referred above.
I am of the opinion that interest of justice would be served by taking a lenient view.
Accordingly, the order on sentence is modified to the extent that sentence of appellant is reduced to imprisonment which he has already undergone.
As appellant has compensated the complainant to the tune of Rs. 2,50,000/- during trial and Rs. 10,000/- during hearing of appeal, the compensation part in the impugned order is set aside.
Appeal is disposed of accordingly.
As appellant has already undergone the sentence, he is released unconditionally.
18. Bail bond and surety bond are discharged.
Copy of judgment along with trial court record be returned to the Trial Court.
Copy of judgment be supplied free of cost to the appellant.
